'''Li Aizhen''' ({{zh|s=李爱珍}}; born May 1936) is a Chinese scientist at the Chinese Academy of Sciences Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology ({{Lang-zh|s=中国科学院上海微系统与信息技术研究所}}). An expert in semiconductor material, she was elected a foreign associate of the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2007.

==Biography==
Born in Guangbian Village, Yongning Town, [[Shishi City|Shishi]], [[Fujian Province]], Li graduated from [[Quanzhou]] First High School in 1954, and entered [[Fudan University]] to study chemistry. She started her research career at Shanghai Institute of Metallurgy of CAS—now Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology—in 1958. From August 1980 to October 1982, Li was a visiting scholar at department of electronic engineering of [[Carnegie-Mellon University]] in the United States. During her stay in the States, she visited [[Bell Labs]] and met with [[Alfred Y. Cho]], the "father of [[molecular beam epitaxy]]".

On May 1, 2007, Li was elected a foreign associate of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS),<ref>[http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=05012007 72 New Members Chosen by Academy]</ref> thus became the first female Chinese scientist to receive this honor. As of 2018 Li has not been admitted into the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS), and is the only non-academician from China who has been elected into the NAS as a foreign associate. She is also a recipient of the 2004 [[List of TWAS Prize laureates|Academy of Sciences for the Developing World (TWAS) Prize in Engineering Sciences]].<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards |title=Prizes and Awards |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Li has made substantial contributions to the development of electronic devices and laser technology.<ref name="bee20">{{cite news |author1=Zhu Hong |title=Li Aizhen Elected Foreign Associate of US National Academy of Sciences |url=http://www.womenofchina.cn/womenofchina/html1/people/Crowd/7/8070-1.htm |accessdate=4 March 2020 |work=womenofchina.cn}}</ref> 

==Honours and awards==
*2003 Member of the Asia Pacific Academy of Materials (APAM)<ref name="bee20"/>
*2004 [[List of TWAS Prize laureates|Academy of Sciences for the Developing World (TWAS) Prize in Engineering Sciences]]<ref name="bee20"/>
*May 2007 Foreign associate of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS)<ref name="bee20"/>
